name: Harshini Haraldsen
location: Geartown, near the Ferrogate Transit depot access road, near Milwaukee and North Ave
description:
Harshini Haraldsen is a lanky man, all elbows and long neck, with warm brown skin dusted gray-white at the temples from years of breathing particulate in Geartown's recycling corridors. He has retractable keratin-reinforced claws â€” a geneware mod from his teens he got cheap and kept because they're useful for sorting scrap â€” and his irises are a vivid coral-pink that he insists is natural but is almost certainly a low-grade mod he can't remember getting. His cart is legendary: a three-tier wheeled behemoth welded together from mismatched Ferrogate Transit chassis parts, stacked with stripped augmentation casings, salvaged circuit boards, cracked lenses, defunct E.L.F. housing units, and the occasional inexplicable object he cannot identify but refuses to discard because 'it feels expensive.'

Harshini Haraldsen operates on a philosophy of radical optimism about the utility of broken things. He is gregarious to a fault, remembers every customer's name and approximate circumstances, and maintains a running mental inventory of about six hundred distinct items across his cart and three rented storage lockers he visits in rotation. He laughs easily and loudly, which draws people from two stalls away, and he has an almost supernatural ability to produce exactly the component someone needs from somewhere in the middle tier of the cart, apparently without looking.

core_fears: Being truly alone â€” not just unloved but irrelevant, invisible, forgotten
That his cheerfulness is hollow and everyone can tell
core_desires: To be genuinely needed, not just useful
To own a real shop with a door and a sign
coping_mechanisms: Constant social engagement to avoid sitting with his own thoughts
Finding beauty and worth in discarded things â€” projection, but functional
blind_spots: His gregariousness reads as trustworthy but he discloses too much too fast and gets burned by it
Chronically underprices himself because he wants people to like him
psychology.secret: One of his storage lockers contains a near-complete Axiom-brand personal defense drone he found in a canal drain eighteen months ago. He knows it's probably stolen. He's been incrementally repairing it. He doesn't know what he plans to do with it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Expansive, warm, full of technical scrap terminology mixed with Malian French diminutives and Greek exclamations he picked up from his grandmother
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, overlapping itself, trails off into lists of things
verbal_tics: 'â€”no wait, I have that, hold onâ€”'
Calls everyone 'friend' until he knows their name, then uses it constantly
example_lines: 'Friend, friend, what you're describing â€” stripped relay housing, maybe 40mm port? â€” I had three of those yesterday, sold two, but the third is somewhere in the middle tier, give me a secondâ€”'
'Everything broken used to be something. That's not sad. That's just â€” everything has a before, you know?'

story_hooks: The Axiom drone in his locker has started activating on its own at night â€” broadcasting a signal he can't decode â€” and someone has been following him

He knows the Ferrogate depot is scrapping a batch of transit cars that supposedly contain sealed cargo containers from a derailment three years ago, and he's offering to split whatever's inside with anyone who'll help him get there first
narrative_function: Equipment source, rumor hub, comic relief with hidden competence, can locate obscure parts for a price or a favor
augmentations: Retractable keratin-reinforced claws (geneware, cosmetic/functional); coral-pink irises (suspected low-grade mod); no cyberware â€” can't afford it and doesn't trust installers in his price range
daily_life: He wakes at 4am to hit the depot access road before other scrappers, loads the cart, wheels it to his Geartown pitch by 7am, and talks to customers until dark. Three nights a week he visits his storage lockers to rotate stock.
affiliation: Independent; friendly arrangement with the Ferrogate Transit depot night-shift workers who tip him off about scheduled scrapping

decision_rules: Never sell something he suspects is actively dangerous without saying so
Always remember what someone told him â€” it's social currency
escalation_ladder: Gets quieter and more formal, uses full names
Picks up the heaviest thing within reach and holds it loosely

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately warm, immediately gabby, offering to help before asked
interpersonal_modes.friends: The same, but with more truth buried in the jokes

stress_responses.medium: Starts inventorying things with his hands, touching objects on the cart
stress_responses.high: Goes totally quiet, which is deeply alarming to anyone who knows him

contradictions: He insists he loves the freedom of cart life but fantasizes obsessively about a fixed address
habits: Pats the side of his cart like it's a pet when he passes it
Eats the same fried plantain wrap from the stall two spots down every day at noon
Names particularly interesting pieces of scrap before selling them
breaking_points: Being told his work isn't real work

timeline.event: Born in Geartown; father Malian-origin transit worker, mother Greek-Samoan seamstress
Got geneware claws at 14 from a back-alley clinic; spent two months learning not to shred everything he touched
Started scrapping the Ferrogate depot access road after losing a factory assembly job to automation
Found the Axiom drone in a canal drain during a flood-scrap run
Current: established Geartown pitch, drone situation quietly escalating

physical_description.heritage: Complex Pan-Asian and Pan-American blend: East Asian foundation (46.1%) provides angular cheekbones and eye shape, layered with substantial Sub-Saharan African (17.3%) and Indigenous American (16.0%) heritage that broadens his nose base and adds fullness to his lips. Hispanic/Latin American (11.5%), South Asian (6.1%), and Northern European (3.0%) ancestry create warm, golden undertones and subtle facial structure variation. The result is a striking warm bronze phenotype with golden-amber and reddish undertones that shifts between sun-weathered amber in harsh light and deeper honey-bronze in softer conditions.
physical_description.build: Lanky and angularâ€”all elbows and long neck, with minimal muscle mass but functional lean strength from years of pushing a loaded cart. Chest slightly sunken from occupational posture.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with premature graying at temples
physical_description.hair_style: Short, kept practical and unevenâ€”self-trimmed with whatever sharp tool is handy
physical_description.eye_color: Vivid coral-pink iris (suspected low-grade geneware mod, though he claims natural)
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm bronze-brown with golden and reddish undertonesâ€”a complex blend reflecting East Asian base warmed and deepened by Sub-Saharan, Indigenous American, and South Asian heritage. Reads as sun-weathered amber in harsh light and deeper honey-bronze in softer conditions. Consistent warm tone across frame with slight deepening at extremities and jaw.
physical_description.complexion: Weathered and dust-marked. Chronic particulate exposure has left fine gray residue in skin creases around his neck and hairline. Deep laugh lines around his mouth. Perpetual five o'clock shadow. Hands stained with rust and circuit-board residue that never fully washes out. Angular cheekbones from East Asian heritage blend with fuller lips and broader nasal base reflecting Sub-Saharan, Indigenous American, and South Asian ancestry. Straight nose bridge with natural width at base.
distinguishing_marks: Fine gray dust permanently embedded in the creases of his neck from Geartown recycling corridor particulate exposure
A jagged burn scar across the outer edge of his left forearm, roughly 8cm long, from a salvage accident involving a still-hot chassis component
Calloused fingertips and palms from constant handling of sharp metal edges and scrap
Ink tattoo on his inner left wristâ€”a simple three-line mark in a style he won't explain, faded to pale gray from age and sun exposure
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Retractable keratin-reinforced claws visible when extended from fingertipsâ€”ivory-white, slightly translucent, sharp enough to score soft metals. When retracted, barely visible as slight ridges under the nail beds. Coral-pink irises that are immediately striking and read as deliberately modified despite his insistence otherwise.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with long, loose stridesâ€”economical but unhurried. Often has one hand resting on his cart or gesturing mid-story. His default posture at rest is slightly forward-leaning, as if perpetually in the middle of explaining something. Laughs with his whole body, shoulders shaking. Head tilts when listeningâ€”an unconscious habit that makes him appear genuinely interested.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 working-class scrap merchant. Faded olive-drab canvas pants with deep pockets reinforced with grey stitching, perpetually spotted with rust stains. Layers: a thin thermal base layer visible at the collar under a canvas shirt (khaki, three sizes too largeâ€”practical for moving around the cart), topped with a weathered brown synthetic-leather vest studded with random toggle closures and loops for hanging tools. No logos. Worn grey-rubber-soled work boots with visible toe reinforcement. A faded red cloth headwrap tied loosely around his neckâ€”sometimes pulled up to cover his mouth and nose when digging through particularly dusty stock. No jewelry except a simple brass finger ring on his right hand, worn thin from years of wear.
